node_tlr_prr_signaling.title: Pattern Recognition Receptors (PRRs) & Toll-Like Receptors (TLRs 1–10)
node_tlr_prr_signaling.subtitle: Plasma Membrane vs. Endosomal PAMP Sensing & MyD88 vs. TRIF Adapter Dual Axes

metrics.extracellular_domain: Horseshoe-shaped Leucine-Rich Repeats (LRRs) that bind PAMPs/DAMPs
metrics.intracellular_domain: TIR Domain (Toll / IL-1 Receptor domain) that recruits MyD88 or TRIF

mechanism: Innate immune cells (macrophages, dendritic cells, neutrophils) use germline-encoded **Pattern Recognition Receptors (PRRs)** to detect conserved microbial **PAMPs** (Pathogen-Associated Molecular Patterns) and host necrotic **DAMPs**.

**CELL SURFACE TLRs (Sense Microbial Membrane Components)**: **TLR4** (with MD-2/CD14) senses Gram-negative **LPS**; **TLR2** (heterodimer with TLR1 or TLR6) senses peptidoglycan/lipopeptides; **TLR5** senses bacterial **Flagellin**.
**ENDOSOMAL TLRs (Sense Nucleic Acids Inside Acidified Endosomes)**: **TLR3** senses viral **dsRNA**; **TLR7 & TLR8** sense viral **ssRNA**; **TLR9** senses unmethylated bacterial/viral **CpG DNA**.

**ADAPTER RULE**: Almost all TLRs signal through **MyD88** (activating IRAK4/TRAF6 $\rightarrow$ **NF-κB** pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) **EXCEPT TLR3**, which signals exclusively through **TRIF** (activating TBK1 $\rightarrow$ **IRF3** $\rightarrow$ **Type I Interferons IFN-α/β**)! Note: **TLR4** is unique in using **BOTH MyD88** (at the plasma membrane) and **TRIF** (after endocytosis)!
csir_high_yield: Master CSIR NET Part B/C TLR Ligand & Adapter Matching Table:
• **TLR3** = Viral **dsRNA** (Poly I:C) | **Endosomal** | Uses **TRIF ONLY** (MyD88-independent!).
• **TLR4** = Gram-negative **Lipopolysaccharide (LPS / Lipid A)** | **Surface/Endosome** | Uses **BOTH MyD88 & TRIF**.
• **TLR5** = Bacterial **Flagellin** | **Surface** | Uses **MyD88**.
• **TLR7/8** = Viral **ssRNA** | **Endosomal** | Uses **MyD88**.
• **TLR9** = Unmethylated **CpG Dinucleotides** | **Endosomal** | Uses **MyD88**.

• **cGAS–STING Pathway**: Cytosolic dsDNA binds **cGAS**, which synthesizes the cyclic dinucleotide **2'3'-cGAMP** (contains a mixed 2'-5' and 3'-5' phosphodiester linkage!) to activate ER-resident **STING $\rightarrow$ TBK1 $\rightarrow$ IRF3 $\rightarrow$ IFN-β**.
pathology: Endotoxic Septic Shock: Systemic Gram-negative bacteremia hyperactivates macrophage **TLR4**, triggering a lethal 'cytokine storm' of **TNF-α** and **IL-1β** that causes vasodilation, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and hypotensive multi-organ collapse.
lab_workbench: Chloroquine / Bafilomycin A1 Endosomal Acidification Assay: Adding Chloroquine blocks endosomal acidification and completely abolishes signaling by **TLR3, TLR7, TLR8, and TLR9** (which require acid-dependent cathepsin cleavage in endosomes), while leaving surface **TLR2/4/5** signaling intact!

node_complement_cascade.title: The Complement System: Classical, Lectin & Alternative Pathways
node_complement_cascade.subtitle: Convergent C3 Convertase Proteolysis, Opsonization (C3b), Anaphylatoxins (C3a/C5a) & MAC Pore

metrics.classical_c3_convertase: C4b2a (Triggered by C1qrs binding to IgM or IgG1/IgG3 immune complexes)
metrics.lectin_c3_convertase: C4b2a (Triggered by MBL + MASP-1/2 binding to microbial Mannose)
metrics.alternative_c3_convertase: C3bBb (Triggered by spontaneous C3 tick-over + Factor B + Factor D + Properdin)
metrics.membrane_attack_complex: C5b + C6 + C7 + C8 + Polymeric C9 ring (10–18 C9 subunits punch a 10 nm lytic pore)

mechanism: Three distinct initiation pathways converge on a single master step—the formation of a **C3 Convertase** that cleaves abundant serum **C3** into **C3a** (anaphylatoxin) and **C3b** (covalent thioester opsonin):

1. **Classical Pathway**: **C1q** binds the Fc region of antigen-bound **IgM** (most potent, pentameric) or **IgG** (requires at least 2 adjacent IgG molecules), activating serine proteases C1r $\rightarrow$ C1s to cleave C4 and C2 into the C3 convertase **C4b2a**.

2. **Lectin Pathway (Antibody-Independent)**: **Mannose-Binding Lectin (MBL)** binds terminal mannose on pathogen surfaces and activates **MASP-1/MASP-2** to cleave C4 and C2 into the identical C3 convertase **C4b2a**.

3. **Alternative Pathway (Innate Amplification Loop)**: Spontaneous hydrolysis of the internal thioester bond in C3 allows **C3b** to bind microbial surfaces, recruit **Factor B**, and be cleaved by **Factor D** into the C3 convertase **C3bBb** (stabilized by **Properdin**).

**TERMINAL LYTIC PATHWAY**: Adding another C3b to either C3 convertase creates the **C5 Convertase** (**C4b2a3b** or **C3bBb3b**), which cleaves C5 into **C5a** (potent neutrophil chemoattractant) and **C5b**. C5b recruits **C6, C7, C8, and 10–18 molecules of C9** to insert the barrel-shaped **Membrane Attack Complex (MAC)** pore, lysing Gram-negative bacteria!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield Complement Exam Rules (CSIR Part B/C Favorites):

• **Which Immunoglobulin is the single most potent activator of the Classical Pathway?** Pentameric **IgM** (a single bound IgM molecule in its 'staple' conformation provides multiple adjacent Fc sites for C1q, whereas monomeric **IgG** requires two IgG molecules to land side-by-side; **IgG4, IgA, and IgE do NOT fix C1q!**).

• **Why doesn't Complement lyse our own healthy Red Blood Cells?** Host cells express GPI-anchored regulatory proteins **CD55 (DAF — Decay-Accelerating Factor, which dissociates C3 convertases)** and **CD59 (Protectin, which blocks C9 polymerization into the MAC)**, plus surface sialic acid that binds **Factor H** to degrade C3b (via Factor I)!

• **Neisseria Susceptibility**: Genetic deficiency in terminal MAC components (**C5, C6, C7, C8, or C9**) causes selective, recurrent infections specifically with Gram-negative diplococci ***Neisseria meningitidis*** and ***Neisseria gonorrhoeae***!
pathology: **Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH)**: Acquired somatic mutation in the **PIGA** gene in a hematopoietic stem cell prevents synthesis of **GPI (Glycosylphosphatidylinositol) anchors**. Red blood cells lack GPI-anchored **CD55 (DAF)** and **CD59**, causing spontaneous complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis at night (treated with the anti-C5 monoclonal antibody **Eculizumab**!).
**Hereditary Angioedema (HAE)**: Deficiency of **C1 Esterase Inhibitor (C1-INH)** causes uncontrolled C1s/kallikrein activation and bradykinin-driven mucosal edema.
lab_workbench: CH50 (50% Hemolytic Complement) Assay: Serial dilutions of patient serum are incubated with sheep red blood cells coated with anti-sheep antibodies (**EA / Hemolysin**); spectrophotometric measurement of released hemoglobin at 412 nm tests the functional integrity of the entire Classical + Terminal MAC cascade (C1 through C9).

node_nk_missing_self.title: Natural Killer (NK) Cells: 'Missing-Self' MHC-I Recognition & ADCC
node_nk_missing_self.subtitle: Inhibitory ITIM vs. Activating ITAM Balance, CD16 FcγRIIIa & Perforin/Granzyme Lysis

metrics.lineage_markers: CD56+ CD16+ CD3- Innate Lymphoid Cells (Lack rearranged TCR or BCR!)
metrics.inhibitory_receptors: KIRs (Killer Ig-like Receptors) & CD94/NKG2A (Contain cytoplasmic ITIMs; bind self MHC Class I)
metrics.activating_receptors: NKG2D (binds stress ligands MICA/MICB) & CD16 / FcγRIIIa (binds IgG Fc for ADCC)
metrics.cytotoxic_payload: Perforin (Ca2+-dependent pore former) + Granzyme B (Serine protease cleaving Bid & Caspase-3)

mechanism: While CD8+ Cytotoxic T Lymphocytes (CTLs) require **MHC Class I** to kill a virus-infected or tumor cell, many viruses (e.g., Herpesviruses, CMV) and cancers evade CTLs by **downregulating surface MHC Class I**.
**KLAS KARRE'S 'MISSING-SELF' HYPOTHESIS**: NK cells integrate signals from two opposing receptor sets:

1. **Inhibitory Receptors (KIRs / NKG2A)**: Recognize normal self **MHC Class I**. When MHC-I is present on a healthy host cell, the cytoplasmic **ITIM** (Immunoreceptor Tyrosine-based Inhibitory Motif) recruits phosphatases **SHP-1/SHP-2**, dominantly **vetoing** NK cell degranulation.
2. **Activating Receptors (NKG2D)**: Recognize stress-induced ligands (**MICA/MICB**) on infected/tumor cells via **ITAM/DAP10** signaling.

**OUTCOME**: If a virus-infected or tumor cell **loses MHC Class I ('Missing Self')** while expressing stress ligands, the inhibitory brake is lost and the NK cell releases **Perforin** and **Granzyme B** (which enters the target cell and directly cleaves **Bid $\rightarrow$ tBid** and **Procaspase-3** to trigger apoptosis!).
csir_high_yield: CTL vs. NK Cell Target Recognition Contrast (Classic CSIR NET Part C Table):
• **Virus-Infected Cell with High MHC-I + Viral Peptide**: Killed by **CD8+ CTL**; spared by **NK Cell**.
• **Virus-Infected / Tumor Cell that Downregulates MHC-I**: Evades **CD8+ CTL**; killed by **NK Cell** ('Missing-Self')!

• **Normal Uninfected Red Blood Cell (Lacks MHC-I)**: Why don't NK cells kill our own RBCs even though RBCs lack MHC Class I? Because RBCs ALSO lack **activating ligands** (like MICA/MICB) and express inhibitory CD47!

• **ADCC (Antibody-Dependent Cell-Mediated Cytotoxicity)**: NK cells express **CD16 (FcγRIIIa)**, which binds the **Fc region of IgG1/IgG3** coating a target cell (e.g., Rituximab-coated B-lymphoma or Trastuzumab-coated HER2+ breast cancer cell), triggering direct Perforin/Granzyme killing!
pathology: Chediak-Higashi Syndrome: Autosomal recessive mutation in the lysosomal trafficking regulator gene **LYST** prevents fusion/exocytosis of lytic granules in NK cells and CTLs (as well as phagolysosomes in neutrophils), causing recurrent pyogenic infections, partial oculocutaneous albinism, and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
lab_workbench: CD107a (LAMP-1) Degranulation FACS Assay & 51Cr-Release Assay against MHC-I-Deficient **K562 Erythroleukemia** Target Cells: K562 cells completely lack MHC Class I, making them the gold-standard universal positive-control target cell line to measure human NK cell cytotoxicity in vitro.

node_ig_structure_isotypes.title: Immunoglobulin Architecture: Heavy/Light Chains, CDRs, Proteolysis & Isotypes
node_ig_structure_isotypes.subtitle: Papain (2 Fab + 1 Fc) vs. Pepsin (F(ab')2) Cleavage & Functional Properties of IgG, IgM, IgA, IgE, IgD

metrics.monomer_formula: H2L2 Heterotetramer (~150 kDa): 2 Identical Heavy Chains (~50 kDa) + 2 Identical Light Chains (κ or λ, ~25 kDa)
metrics.immunoglobulin_fold: ~110-aa β-barrel sandwich (2 antiparallel β-sheets stabilized by an intrachain disulfide bond)
metrics.paratope_cdrs: 3 Hypervariable Complementarity-Determining Regions (CDR1, CDR2, CDR3) on VH + 3 on VL = 6 CDR loops per binding site

mechanism: An antibody monomer consists of two identical **Heavy (H) chains** and two identical **Light (L) chains** (**either Kappa κ OR Lambda λ, never both** on the same molecule!) linked by interchain disulfide bonds at the flexible proline-rich **Hinge Region** ( note: **IgM and IgE lack a hinge region** and instead possess an extra constant domain, $\text{C}_\text{H}4$!).
**CLASSICAL PROTEOLYTIC DIGESTION (Rodney Porter & Gerald Edelman Nobel Experiments)**:

• **Papain Digestion** (cuts **ABOVE** the inter-heavy-chain disulfide bonds): Yields **3 fragments of ~50 kDa each** $\rightarrow$ **two monovalent Fab fragments** (bind antigen, CANNOT precipitate/crosslink!) and **one crystallizable Fc fragment** (mediates effector functions: complement C1q, Fc receptors, placental FcRn).

• **Pepsin Digestion** (cuts **BELOW** the inter-heavy-chain disulfide bonds): Yields **one bivalent $\text{F(ab')}_2$ fragment** (~100 kDa; **CAN still crosslink and precipitate antigen!**) while digesting the Fc tail into small peptides (**pFc'**).
• **β-Mercaptoethanol (β-ME) Reduction**: Reduces interchain disulfide bonds, separating H chains (50 kDa) and L chains (25 kDa) on reducing SDS-PAGE.
csir_high_yield: Master CSIR NET Five Immunoglobulin Isotypes Comparison:

• **IgG (γ)**: Most abundant in serum (~75–80%); highest half-life (~21–23 days via **FcRn** neonatal receptor recycling); **ONLY isotype that crosses the human placenta** (IgG1, IgG3, IgG4 cross; IgG2 poorly); opsonizes via FcγR.

• **IgM (μ)**: First antibody produced in a primary immune response and first expressed on naive B cells (monomeric mIgM); secreted as a **900 kDa Pentamer** (held by a **J-chain**; 10 theoretical binding sites / valence = 10, effective valence = 5 for bulky antigens); **highest avidity** and **most efficient C1q complement activator** per molecule.

• **IgA (α)**: Most abundant antibody produced across the entire body by total daily synthesis! Secreted across mucosal epithelia (gut, tears, saliva, colostrum/breast milk) as a **400 kDa Dimer** held by a **J-chain** and wrapped in a **Secretory Component** (cleaved ectodomain of the **Polymeric Ig Receptor / pIgR**, which protects dimeric sIgA from luminal gastrointestinal proteases!).

• **IgE (ε)**: Lowest serum concentration (~0.002%); contains 4 constant domains ($\text{C}_\varepsilon 1–4$, no hinge); binds with ultra-high affinity ($K_d \approx 10^{-10}\ \text{M}$) to **FcεRI** on **Mast Cells and Basophils** (mediates **Type I Immediate Hypersensitivity / Anaphylaxis** and defense against **Helminth parasites** alongside eosinophils).
• **IgD (δ)**: Co-expressed with monomeric IgM on mature naive B cells (generated by **alternative RNA splicing** of a single primary VDJ-$\text{C}_\mu$-$\text{C}_\delta$ transcript!).

• **Idiotype vs. Allotype vs. Isotype**: **Isotype** = Constant-region class differences present in all members of a species (IgG vs. IgM); **Allotype** = Allelic intraspecies polymorphism in constant regions (e.g., Gm alleles); **Idiotype** = Unique antigenic determinants of the hypervariable **CDR / antigen-binding paratope** of a single B-cell clone!
pathology: Multiple Myeloma & **Bence-Jones Proteins**: Malignant proliferation of a single plasma cell clone produces a monoclonal 'M-spike' on serum protein electrophoresis and excretes free monoclonal **Light Chains (κ or λ)** in the urine (**Bence-Jones proteins**, which precipitate at 50–60°C and redissolve at 90–100°C!).
lab_workbench: Affinity vs. Avidity Equilibrium Dialysis (Scatchard Plot): **Affinity** is the strength of a single paratope-epitope bond ($K_a = [\text{Ab}\cdot\text{Ag}] / ([\text{Ab}][\text{Ag}])$), whereas **Avidity** is the combined synergistic strength of multivalent binding (Pentameric IgM has low intrinsic affinity per Fab arm but massive overall avidity!).

node_vdj_rag_recombination.title: Somatic V(D)J Recombination: The 12/23 Rule, RAG1/2, Artemis & TdT
node_vdj_rag_recombination.subtitle: Susumu Tonegawa's Combinatorial & Junctional Diversity Engine in Developing B & T Cells

metrics.heavy_chain_loci: V (Variable) + D (Diversity) + J (Joining) segments (Chromosome 14 in humans; join D-to-J first, then V-to-DJ!)
metrics.light_chain_loci: V + J segments ONLY (Zero D segments in Kappa [Chr 2] or Lambda [Chr 22] light chains!)
metrics.rss_architecture: Conserved Heptamer (5'-CACAGTG-3') + 12 bp or 23 bp Non-Conserved Spacer + Conserved Nonamer (5'-ACAAAAACC-3')
metrics.junctional_enzymes: RAG1/RAG2 (Hairpin cleavage) -> Ku70/80 + DNA-PKcs + Artemis (Hairpin nicking -> P-nucleotides) -> TdT (Untemplated N-nucleotides)

mechanism: Because the human genome contains <20,000 genes yet produces $>10^{11}$ distinct antibodies and TCRs, developing B cells (in Bone Marrow) and T cells (in Thymus) somatically rearrange germline **Variable (V), Diversity (D), and Joining (J)** gene segments (**Susumu Tonegawa's 1987 Nobel Discovery**).

**THE 12/23 RECOMBINATION RULE**: Each gene segment is flanked by a **Recombination Signal Sequence (RSS)** consisting of a conserved **7-bp Heptamer** and **9-bp Nonamer** separated by either a **12-bp spacer** (1 helical turn) or a **23-bp spacer** (2 helical turns). **A 12-RSS can ONLY recombine with a 23-RSS!** (In the Ig Heavy chain locus: $V_H$ has a 23-RSS, $D_H$ has 12-RSS on both sides, and $J_H$ has a 23-RSS—which guarantees that $V_H$ can NEVER join directly to $J_H$, skipping $D_H$!).
**FOUR-STEP ENZYMATIC MECHANISM (Antigen-Independent!)**:

1. **RAG1 / RAG2 Synapsis & Hairpin Formation**: Lymphoid-specific **RAG1 and RAG2** nick one strand precisely between the coding segment and the RSS heptamer; the liberated 3'-OH attacks the opposite strand to create a **covalently sealed Coding Hairpin** and a blunt **Signal End**.

2. **P-Nucleotides (Palindromic)**: **Ku70/Ku80** and **DNA-PKcs** recruit the endonuclease **Artemis**, which nicks the coding hairpin asymmetrically off-center. Repair polymerase fills in the single-stranded overhang, generating short **Palindromic (P) nucleotides**.

3. **N-Nucleotides (Non-Templated)**: **Terminal Deoxynucleotidyl Transferase (TdT)**—a template-independent DNA polymerase active primarily during Heavy Chain rearrangement—randomly adds up to 15–20 untemplated **N-nucleotides** to the 3' ends (making **CDR3** the most hypervariable loop in the entire antibody!).
4. **Ligation**: **XRCC4 + DNA Ligase IV (NHEJ)** seals the coding joint.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Traps on Antibody Diversity & Allelic Exclusion:

• **Which chains have D (Diversity) segments?** **Ig Heavy Chain ($\text{IgH}$)**, **TCR $\beta$ chain**, and **TCR $\delta$ chain**. (**Ig Light chains [$\kappa, \lambda$], TCR $\alpha$, and TCR $\gamma$ contain ONLY V and J segments—ZERO D segments!**).

• **Order of Rearrangement & Allelic Exclusion**: In a pro-B cell, the **Heavy Chain locus rearranges FIRST** ($D_H$-to-$J_H$, then $V_H$-to-$D_HJ_H$). If productive, the $\mu$ heavy chain pairs with the surrogate light chain (VpreB/$\lambda 5$) to form the **pre-BCR**, which signals the **permanent epigenetic shutdown of the other parental Heavy Chain allele (Allelic Exclusion!)** and triggers $\kappa$ Light Chain rearrangement (and only if both $\kappa$ alleles fail does $\lambda$ rearrange = **Isotypic Exclusion**). This guarantees every B cell is **monospecific**!

• **Does Somatic Hypermutation occur in T-Cell Receptors (TCRs)?** **NO!** Both B cells and T cells undergo **V(D)J recombination** (via RAG1/2), but **ONLY B cells** undergo **Somatic Hypermutation and Class Switch Recombination** (via AID)! Why? Because if a T cell mutated its TCR after thymic selection, it could accidentally lose MHC restriction or become fatally self-reactive!
pathology: **Omenn Syndrome & RAG1/RAG2-Deficient SCID**: Complete loss of *RAG1* or *RAG2* abolishes V(D)J recombination in both B and T lineages, causing **T(–) B(–) NK(+) Severe Combined Immunodeficiency** (NK cells are normal because they do not use V(D)J recombination!).
lab_workbench: Southern Blot Proof of Somatic DNA Rearrangement (Tonegawa's Classic Experiment): Digesting embryonic/non-lymphoid liver DNA vs. B-cell myeloma DNA with a restriction enzyme (BamHI) and hybridizing with radiolabeled V and C cDNA probes reveals that V and C segments lie on separate restriction fragments in germline DNA, but migrate on a **single fused restriction fragment** in mature B cells!

node_aid_shm_csr.title: Germinal Center Reactions: AID, Somatic Hypermutation (SHM) & Class Switch Recombination (CSR)
node_aid_shm_csr.subtitle: Antigen-Driven Cytidine Deamination (C -> U), Affinity Maturation & Constant-Region Looping

metrics.master_enzyme: AID (Activation-Induced Cytidine Deaminase — expressed ONLY in activated Germinal Center B cells!)
metrics.chemical_reaction: Deaminates deoxycytidine (dC) into deoxyuridine (dU) on single-stranded transcribed DNA (R-loops)
metrics.costimulatory_trigger: T-Follicular Helper (Tfh) cell CD40L (CD154) binding to B-cell CD40 receptor + Cytokines (IL-4, TGF-β, IFN-γ)

mechanism: Unlike V(D)J recombination (which occurs in the bone marrow **before** antigen contact), **Somatic Hypermutation (SHM)** and **Class Switch Recombination (CSR)** occur in peripheral lymph node **Germinal Centers AFTER antigen stimulation** and require **CD4+ T-cell help (CD40L binding to B-cell CD40)**.
Both processes are initiated by a single B-cell-specific enzyme: **AID (Activation-Induced Cytidine Deaminase)**, which converts **Cytosine (C) into Uracil (U)** in actively transcribed DNA:

1. **SOMATIC HYPERMUTATION (Affinity Maturation)**: AID targets the rearranged $V(D)J$ variable exon at $10^{-3}$ mutations/bp/generation ($10^6$-fold higher than background!). **Uracil-DNA Glycosylase (UNG)** and error-prone mismatch/BER polymerases (Pol $\eta$) convert the U:G lesions into point mutations in the CDR loops. B cells whose mutated BCR binds antigen held on **Follicular Dendritic Cells (FDCs)** with higher affinity survive, while low-affinity clones die by apoptosis.

2. **CLASS SWITCH RECOMBINATION (Isotype Switching)**: AID deaminates GC-rich repetitive **Switch (S) regions** located upstream of each Heavy Chain constant gene ($S_\mu, S_\gamma, S_\alpha, S_\varepsilon$). UNG + APE1 create double-strand breaks in two Switch regions; the intervening constant genes (e.g., $C_\mu$ and $C_\delta$) are **looped out and permanently deleted as an excised circular DNA**, joining the **exact same $V_HD_HJ_H$ variable exon** to a downstream constant region ($C_\gamma, C_\alpha$, or $C_\varepsilon$)!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR Part C Distinctions on Class Switching:

• **Does Class Switching change the antigen specificity (idiotype) or Light Chain of the antibody?** **NO!** The $V_HD_HJ_H$ exon and the entire Light Chain remain **100% identical**; ONLY the Heavy Chain Constant region ($C_H$) changes (changing effector function from IgM to IgG, IgA, or IgE).
• **Cytokine Signals Dictating Isotype Switch**:
– **IL-4** (from $\text{T}_\text{H}2$ / $\text{T}_{\text{fh}}$) drives switching to **IgE** and **IgG1/IgG4**.
– **TGF-β** (+ IL-5 / BAFF in Peyer's patches) drives switching to **IgA**.
– **IFN-γ** (from $\text{T}_\text{H}1$) drives switching to **IgG2a / IgG3** (opsonizing/complement-fixing IgGs).

• **Why can a B cell co-express IgM and IgD simultaneously, yet can NEVER switch back to IgM after switching to IgG?** Co-expression of IgM + IgD uses **reversible alternative RNA splicing** of a long primary transcript; switching to IgG/IgA/IgE uses **irreversible DNA deletion** of the $C_\mu/C_\delta$ genes!
pathology: • **Type 1 (X-linked)**: Mutation in **CD40L (CD154)** on T helper cells (cannot activate B-cell CD40 or macrophage CD40).
*Clinical Hallmarks*: Patients have **sky-high serum IgM** alongside **near-zero IgG, IgA, and IgE**, completely lack Germinal Centers, and cannot undergo affinity maturation!
lab_workbench: ELISA Avidity Index Assay (Chaotropic Ammonium Thiocyanate $\text{NH}_4\text{SCN}$ Elution): Measures affinity maturation over the course of vaccination—early primary-response IgG is easily stripped from antigen plates by 1.5 M $\text{NH}_4\text{SCN}$, whereas late germinal-center SHM-matured IgG remains tightly bound.

node_mhc_class_i_pathway.title: MHC Class I Endogenous Pathway: Immunoproteasome, TAP1/2 & CD8+ CTL Restriction
node_mhc_class_i_pathway.subtitle: Polymorphic α-Chain + β2-Microglobulin | Presenting 8–10 aa Cytosolic Peptides to CD8+ T Cells

metrics.expression_pattern: Expressed on ALL nucleated somatic cells (and platelets); ABSENT on mature Mammalian Red Blood Cells!
metrics.quaternary_structure: Polymorphic α-heavy chain (α1, α2, α3 domains; ~45 kDa) non-covalently paired with invariant β2-Microglobulin (12 kDa)
metrics.human_hla_loci: Classical HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C (Mouse H-2K, H-2D, H-2L) on Chromosome 6p21
metrics.peptide_groove: Closed-ended groove formed by α1 + α2 domains; binds strictly short 8–10 amino acid peptides (anchor residues at C-terminus)

mechanism: Designed to report **intracellular pathogens** (viruses, cytosolic bacteria like *Listeria*, and mutated tumor neoantigens) to **CD8+ Cytotoxic T Lymphocytes (CTLs)**.
**STEP-BY-STEP CYTOSOLIC-TO-ER PATHWAY**:

1. **Immunoproteasome Cleavage**: Ubiquitinated endogenous or viral proteins in the cytosol are degraded by the **26S Proteasome** (induced by **IFN-γ** to incorporate **LMP2, LMP7, and MECL-1** catalytic subunits, forming the **Immunoproteasome**, which generates peptides with hydrophobic/basic C-termini ideal for MHC-I!).

2. **TAP1/TAP2 ER Translocation**: Peptides are pumped from the cytosol into the Rough ER lumen by the heterodimeric ATP-binding cassette transporter **TAP1 / TAP2** (Transporter Associated with Antigen Processing).

3. **Peptide-Loading Complex & ERAAP Trimming**: Inside the ER, nascent MHC-I $\alpha$-chains fold with **Calnexin**, bind **$\beta_2$-Microglobulin**, and tether to TAP via **Tapasin**, Calreticulin, and ERp57. **ERAAP (ERAP1)** aminopeptidase trims the peptide N-terminus to the exact **8–10 amino acid** length so it snaps into the closed $\alpha_1/\alpha_2$ groove, licensing export via the Golgi to the plasma membrane!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Experimental Scenarios on MHC Class I:

• **What happens in a $\beta_2$-Microglobulin ($\beta_2\text{m}^{-/-}$) Knockout Mouse or a *TAP1/TAP2*-Mutant Cell Line (e.g., RMA-S cells)?** Without $\beta_2$-microglobulin OR without a loaded 8–10 mer peptide inside the ER, the MHC Class I $\alpha$-chain is **structurally unstable**, fails ER quality control, and **NEVER reaches the cell surface**! Consequently, the mouse completely lacks mature **CD8+ T cells** (while CD4+ T cells and MHC Class II remain 100% normal!).
• **Rule of 8**: **MHC Class I** $\times$ **CD8** = 8 (CD8 coreceptor binds the conserved **$\alpha_3$ domain** of MHC-I).

• **Cross-Presentation Exception**: Classical dendritic cells (cDC1) can take up **exogenous** viral/tumor antigens and route them into the **MHC Class I pathway** ('Cross-Presentation') so they can prime naive CD8+ T cells even if the dendritic cell itself is not infected by the virus!
pathology: **Bare Lymphocyte Syndrome Type I**: Autosomal recessive mutation in **TAP1 or TAP2** abolishes surface MHC Class I expression, causing chronic necrotizing respiratory infections and absence of CD8+ T cells.

**Viral Immune Evasion**: Herpes Simplex Virus (**ICP47**) plugs the cytosolic face of **TAP1/2**; Human Cytomegalovirus (**US6**) blocks TAP ATP binding, while **US2/US11** retrotranslocate MHC-I $\alpha$-chains into the cytosol for ERAD destruction!
lab_workbench: Zinkernagel & Doherty MHC-Restriction 51Cr-Release Assay (1996 Nobel Prize): Virus-specific CD8+ CTLs isolated from an LCMV-infected $H\text{-}2^k$ mouse will lyse LCMV-infected $H\text{-}2^k$ target fibroblasts, but will **NOT** lyse uninfected $H\text{-}2^k$ cells OR LCMV-infected $H\text{-}2^b$ cells—proving that TCRs recognize **BOTH foreign peptide AND self-MHC polymorphism simultaneously**!

node_mhc_class_ii_pathway.title: MHC Class II Exogenous Pathway: Invariant Chain (Ii / CLIP), HLA-DM & CD4+ TH Restriction
node_mhc_class_ii_pathway.subtitle: Polymorphic α/β Heterodimer on Professional APCs | Presenting 13–18+ aa Endosomal Peptides

metrics.expression_pattern: Restricted to Professional Antigen-Presenting Cells (APCs): Dendritic Cells, Macrophages, B Cells (+ Thymic Epithelium)
metrics.quaternary_structure: Polymorphic α-chain (~33 kDa: α1, α2) + Polymorphic β-chain (~28 kDa: β1, β2) — Both chains span the membrane!
metrics.human_hla_loci: Classical HLA-DP, HLA-DQ, HLA-DR (Mouse I-A, I-E); transcription controlled by master regulator CIITA
metrics.peptide_groove: Open-ended groove formed by α1 + β1 domains; accommodates longer 13–18+ amino acid peptides whose ends hang out

mechanism: Designed to report **extracellular pathogens** (phagocytosed bacteria, fungi, parasites, and endocytosed soluble toxins/antigens) to **CD4+ Helper T Cells ($\text{T}_\text{H}$)**.
**WHY DOESN'T MHC CLASS II BIND ENDOGENOUS ER PEPTIDES? (THE INVARIANT CHAIN SWITCH)**:

1. **ER Assembly & Groove Blockade**: Newly synthesized MHC Class II $\alpha\beta$ dimers assemble in the Rough ER (where TAP is pumping millions of cytosolic peptides!). To prevent MHC-II from binding endogenous ER peptides, a trimeric protein called the **Invariant Chain (Ii / CD74)** immediately lays its **CLIP** (Class II-Associated Invariant Chain Peptide) segment directly across the $\alpha_1/\beta_1$ peptide-binding groove AND uses its cytoplasmic sorting signal to route MHC-II away from the secretory pathway into an acidified endolysosomal compartment (**MIIC**).

2. **Endosomal Cathepsin Cleavage**: Meanwhile, extracellular antigens taken up by phagocytosis or receptor-mediated endocytosis are degraded in acidified endolysosomes by acid proteases (**Cathepsins S and L**). Cathepsin S also cleaves the Invariant Chain, leaving **ONLY the short 24-aa CLIP fragment** sitting inside the MHC-II groove.

3. **HLA-DM Peptide Exchange**: The non-classical MHC-like chaperone **HLA-DM** (H-2M in mice) binds MHC-II, pries open the groove to **eject CLIP**, and catalyzes loading of high-affinity exogenous **13–18 aa peptides** (regulated in B cells and thymus by **HLA-DO**). Peptide-loaded MHC-II then traffics to the plasma membrane!
csir_high_yield: Master MHC Class I vs. MHC Class II Comparison & Mutant Phenotypes (Guaranteed CSIR Part C Topic):
• **Rule of 8**: **MHC Class II** $\times$ **CD4** = 8 (CD4 coreceptor binds the non-polymorphic **$\beta_2$ domain** of MHC-II).

• **What happens in an *HLA-DM* Knockout Cell?** MHC Class II molecules reach the cell surface normally at normal levels, **BUT >95% of surface MHC-II grooves remain permanently plugged with the self-peptide CLIP** instead of exogenous foreign peptides!

• **What happens in an Invariant Chain (*Ii / CD74*) Knockout Mouse?** MHC-II molecules misfold in the ER, fail to traffic to endosomes, accidentally bind endogenous ER peptides, and **CD4+ T-cell development collapses**.

• **Chloroquine / Leupeptin Sensitivity**: Treating APCs with **Chloroquine** (raises endosomal pH) or **Leupeptin** (inhibits Cathepsin cysteine proteases) blocks Invariant Chain cleavage and completely abolishes **MHC Class II** presentation while sparing MHC Class I!
pathology: **Bare Lymphocyte Syndrome Type II**: Autosomal recessive mutation in **CIITA** (Class II Transactivator—the master transcriptional coactivator required for IFN-γ-inducible and constitutive MHC-II transcription) or **RFX** factors completely abolishes MHC Class II expression on all APCs, causing severe **CD4+ T-cell deficiency** and hypogammaglobulinemia.
lab_workbench: Mixed Lymphocyte Reaction (MLR) & Peptide-MHC Tetramer Staining: Irradiated stimulator APCs incubated with responder T cells trigger robust allogeneic CD4+ T-cell proliferation (measured by CFSE dilution or 3H-thymidine incorporation) driven primarily by polymorphic **HLA-DR** mismatches.

node_tcr_synapse_costimulation.title: The TCR–CD3 Complex, Two-Signal Costimulation (CD28/B7), Superantigens & Checkpoints
node_tcr_synapse_costimulation.subtitle: ITAM Phosphorylation by Lck/ZAP-70, Clonal Anergy vs. IL-2 Proliferation & CTLA-4/PD-1 Therapy

metrics.tcr_cd3_stoichiometry: αβ TCR Heterodimer (short 5–12 aa tails!) + CD3γε + CD3δε + ζζ Homodimer (Total = 10 ITAMs per TCR complex!)
metrics.signal_1_cascade: TCR + CD4/CD8 -> Lck kinase phosphorylates CD3/ζ ITAMs -> ZAP-70 docks -> LAT/PLCγ1 -> NFAT + NF-κB + AP-1
metrics.signal_2_costimulation: T-cell CD28 binds APC B7-1 (CD80) / B7-2 (CD86) -> PI3K/Akt -> Stabilizes IL-2 mRNA & induces CD25 (IL-2Rα)
metrics.coinhibitory_brakes: CTLA-4 (outcompetes CD28 for B7 with 20x higher affinity) & PD-1 (binds PD-L1/L2; recruits SHP-2 phosphatase)

mechanism: Because the $\alpha\beta$ T-Cell Receptor (TCR) has tiny cytoplasmic tails (5–12 aa), it cannot signal alone. It associates non-covalently with the invariant **CD3 complex** ($\gamma\varepsilon$ and $\delta\varepsilon$ heterodimers) plus a **$\zeta\zeta$ (CD247) homodimer**, which together contribute **10 cytoplasmic ITAMs** (Immunoreceptor Tyrosine-based Activation Motifs).
**THE TWO-SIGNAL MODEL OF NAIVE T-CELL ACTIVATION**:

• **Signal 1 (Antigen-Specific)**: TCR binds Peptide-MHC while the coreceptor (CD4 or CD8) brings its cytoplasmic tail-associated Src kinase **Lck** into the synapse. Lck phosphorylates the CD3/$\zeta$ **ITAMs**, creating docking sites for the tandem-SH2 kinase **ZAP-70**, which activates PLC$\gamma$1 ($\text{Ca}^{2+}\rightarrow\text{Calcineurin}\rightarrow\textbf{NFAT}$; $\text{DAG/PKC}\theta\rightarrow\textbf{NF-\kappa B}$; $\text{Ras/MAPK}\rightarrow\textbf{AP-1}$).

• **Signal 2 (Costimulatory 'Danger' Verification)**: Constitutive **CD28** on the T cell must simultaneously bind **B7-1 (CD80) or B7-2 (CD86)** (upregulated on APCs only after TLR/PAMP sensing!). Signal 1 + Signal 2 drive massive transcription of **IL-2** and the high-affinity **IL-2 Receptor $\alpha$-chain (CD25)**, launching clonal expansion.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR Part C Scenarios on Clonal Anergy, Superantigens & Checkpoint Therapy:

• **What happens if a Naive T Cell receives Signal 1 (TCR-MHC) WITHOUT Signal 2 (CD28-B7 blockade or resting APC)?** The T cell does NOT proliferate and cannot be activated even if restimulated later with full costimulation—it enters permanent functional unresponsiveness called **Clonal Anergy** (mediated by E3 ubiquitin ligases Cbl-b/GRAIL)!

• **Superantigens (Staphylococcal Enterotoxins SEA–SEE, TSST-1)**: Do **NOT** require intracellular processing and do **NOT** bind inside the MHC peptide groove! Instead, an intact Superantigen crosslinks the **outer lateral face of the MHC Class II $\beta$-chain** directly to the **$V_\beta$ domain of the TCR**, polyclonally activating **5–20% of all T cells in the body** at once and causing lethal **Toxic Shock Syndrome**!
• **T-Helper Subset Master Transcription Factors (Memorize for CSIR!)**:
– **$\text{T}_\text{H}1$**: Induced by **IL-12 / IFN-γ** | Master TF = **T-bet** | Secretes **IFN-γ** (activates macrophages).
– **$\text{T}_\text{H}2$**: Induced by **IL-4** | Master TF = **GATA-3** | Secretes **IL-4, IL-5, IL-13** (helminths/allergy).
– **$\text{T}_\text{H}17$**: Induced by **TGF-β + IL-6** | Master TF = **RORγt** | Secretes **IL-17, IL-22** (neutrophil recruitment).
– **$\text{T}_{\text{reg}}$ (Regulatory)**: Induced by **TGF-β + IL-2** | Master TF = **FoxP3** (CD4+ CD25+) | Secretes **IL-10, TGF-β**.
pathology: **IPEX Syndrome**: X-linked mutation in **FOXP3** abolishes Regulatory T cells ($\text{T}_{\text{reg}}$), causing fatal neonatal multi-organ autoimmunity.

**Cancer Immune Checkpoint Blockade (James Allison & Tasuku Honjo 2018 Nobel Prize)**: Monoclonal antibodies blocking **CTLA-4 (Ipilimumab)** or **PD-1 / PD-L1 (Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab)** release the inhibitory brakes on exhausted tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells so they eradicate metastatic melanoma and lung carcinomas!
lab_workbench: ELISpot (Enzyme-Linked ImmunoSpot) & Intracellular Cytokine Staining (ICS with Brefeldin A): Brefeldin A blocks ER-to-Golgi secretion so IFN-γ/IL-4/IL-17 accumulate inside stimulated T cells for single-cell multiparameter FACS enumeration.

node_hybridoma_hat_selection.title: Hybridoma Technology & HAT Medium Biochemical Selection
node_hybridoma_hat_selection.subtitle: Köhler & Milstein PEG Fusion | De Novo (Aminopterin Block) vs. Salvage (HGPRT & TK) Nucleotide Pathways

metrics.fusion_partners: Normal Antigen-Primed Splenic B Cell (HGPRT+, TK+, Antibody+, Mortal) + Myeloma Cell (HGPRT–, Ig–, Immortal)
metrics.fusogen: Polyethylene Glycol (PEG 1500–4000) or Electrofusion (dehydrates lipid bilayers to fuse plasma membranes)
metrics.hat_components: H = Hypoxanthine (Purine salvage substrate) | A = Aminopterin (DHFR inhibitor) | T = Thymidine (Pyrimidine salvage substrate)
metrics.antibody_engineering: Mouse mAb (-omab) -> Chimeric (-ximab) -> CDR-Grafted Humanized (-zumab) -> Fully Human Phage/Transgenic (-umab)

mechanism: Developed by **Georges Köhler and César Milstein (1984 Nobel Prize)** to produce unlimited quantities of a single, monospecific **Monoclonal Antibody (mAb)** directed against a single epitope.
**BIOCHEMICAL LOGIC OF HAT SELECTION MEDIUM**:

Mammalian cells synthesize DNA nucleotides via two routes: (A) The **De Novo Pathway** (which requires **Dihydrofolate Reductase [DHFR]** and Tetrahydrofolate), and (B) The **Salvage Pathway** (which requires the enzyme **HGPRT** [Hypoxanthine-Guanine Phosphoribosyltransferase] to convert **Hypoxanthine** into purines, and **Thymidine Kinase [TK]** to convert **Thymidine** into dTTP).
When **PEG** fuses B cells with **HGPRT-deficient ($\text{HGPRT}^-$) Myeloma cells**, the mixture is plated in **HAT Medium**:
1. **Aminopterin** (folate analog) completely **BLOCKS the De Novo Pathway** in ALL cells, forcing every cell in the dish to rely 100% on the Salvage Pathway.
2. **Unfused Myeloma Cells ($\text{HGPRT}^-$, Immortal)**: **DIE** within days because Aminopterin blocks their de novo synthesis and they lack **HGPRT** to use Hypoxanthine in the salvage pathway!
3. **Unfused Normal B Cells ($\text{HGPRT}^+$, Mortal)**: Survive HAT biochemically, but **DIE naturally within 7–14 days** because primary B cells have a finite lifespan (Hayflick limit) in vitro.

4. **Fused B–Myeloma Hybridomas ($\text{HGPRT}^+$ from B cell + Immortality from Myeloma)**: **THE ONLY CELLS THAT SURVIVE AND PROLIFERATE INDEFINITELY!** Cloned by **limiting dilution** (1 cell/well) and screened by ELISA.
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part B & C Questions on Hybridoma & Therapeutic mAbs:
• **What is the exact role of each letter in HAT?**
– **Aminopterin**: Inhibits **DHFR**, blocking *de novo* synthesis of BOTH purines (IMP) and thymidylate (dTMP).
– **Hypoxanthine**: Rescues **Purine** synthesis via **HGPRT** (donated by the splenic B cell).
– **Thymidine**: Rescues **Pyrimidine (dTTP)** synthesis via **Thymidine Kinase (TK)**.

• **How do you select FOR $\text{HGPRT}^-$ myeloma mutants BEFORE fusion?** Grow myeloma cells in **8-Azaguanine** or **6-Thioguanine (6-TG)**! Wild-type $\text{HGPRT}^+$ cells incorporate toxic 8-azaguanine into DNA and die, whereas $\text{HGPRT}^-$ mutants survive!
• **Therapeutic mAb Nomenclature & HAMA Response**: Injecting pure mouse mAbs into patients triggers a **HAMA (Human Anti-Mouse Antibody)** immune response. To prevent HAMA:
– **Chimeric mAb (e.g., Rituximab, Infliximab)**: Mouse $V_H/V_L$ variable domains fused to Human $C_H/C_L$ constant domains (~65% human).
– **Humanized mAb (e.g., Trastuzumab, Bevacizumab)**: **ONLY the 6 hypervariable CDR loops** from the mouse are grafted onto a human IgG framework (~90–95% human)!
pathology: Clinical Monoclonal Antibody Therapeutics: **Rituximab** (anti-CD20 in B-cell lymphoma), **Trastuzumab** (anti-HER2 in breast cancer), **Adalimumab / Infliximab** (anti-TNF-α in rheumatoid arthritis & Crohn's disease), **Omalizumab** (anti-IgE Fc in severe asthma).
lab_workbench: Limiting Dilution Cloning & Isotyping Strip Assay: Seeding hybridoma cells at statistically 0.3–0.5 cells per 96-well plate (following a Poisson distribution) guarantees monoclonality before scaling up in bioreactors.

node_elisa_lateral_flow.title: Immunodiagnostics: ELISA (Direct, Indirect, Sandwich, Competitive) & Lateral Flow RDTs
node_elisa_lateral_flow.subtitle: HRP/TMB Colorimetric Kinetics, Colloidal Gold Immunochromatography & FACS Gating

metrics.elisa_enzymes: Horseradish Peroxidase (HRP + TMB/H2O2 -> 450 nm yellow after H2SO4 stop) or Alkaline Phosphatase (AP + pNPP -> 405 nm)
metrics.sandwich_requirement: Antigen must be multivalent / large enough to possess at least TWO non-overlapping epitopes (Capture Ab + Detection Ab)
metrics.competitive_curve: Inversely Proportional! Higher free sample antigen = LOWER absorbance signal (Ideal for small haptens/steroids with 1 epitope)
metrics.lateral_flow_zones: Sample Pad -> Conjugate Pad (Colloidal Gold-Ab) -> Nitrocellulose Membrane (Test Line + Control Line) -> Absorbent Wick Pad

mechanism: **FOUR ARCHITECTURES OF ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay)**:

1. **Indirect ELISA (Detects Patient ANTIBODY — e.g., anti-HIV or anti-HCV IgG/IgM screening)**: Viral antigen is coated on the 96-well polystyrene plate $\rightarrow$ Patient serum added $\rightarrow$ Enzyme-conjugated Secondary Anti-Human IgG/IgM added $\rightarrow$ Substrate color is **directly proportional** to patient antibody titer.

2. **Sandwich ELISA (Detects Patient ANTIGEN — e.g., HBsAg, NS1 Dengue, Cytokines, hCG)**: Unlabeled **Capture Antibody** is immobilized on the well $\rightarrow$ Patient sample antigen binds $\rightarrow$ Enzyme-linked **Detection Antibody** binds a second non-overlapping epitope on the antigen (2–5x more sensitive than direct/indirect ELISA!).

3. **Competitive / Inhibition ELISA (Detects Small Haptens/Hormones like Progesterone, Digoxin, Aflatoxin with ONLY 1 epitope)**: Free antigen in the patient sample competes with a fixed amount of reference antigen for limited antibody binding sites. **More free antigen in the patient sample leaves LESS antibody bound to the well = LOWER optical density (Inverse Standard Curve!)**.
**LATERAL FLOW RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TEST (RDT) CASSETTE ARCHITECTURE (e.g., HBsAg / hCG)**:

Liquid sample applied to the **Sample Pad** migrates by capillary action through the **Conjugate Pad**, rehydrating mobile **Colloidal Gold-conjugated monoclonal antibodies (Mouse IgG-AuNP)**. If target antigen (e.g., HBsAg) is present, the Antigen–Gold-Ab complex is captured by immobilized anti-target antibodies at the **Test Line (T)**, forming a visible red/magenta band. Excess unbound Mouse IgG-AuNP continues migrating and is captured by **Goat Anti-Mouse IgG** at the **Control Line (C)**, validating proper capillary flow and reagent integrity!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR Unit 13 Diagnostic Interpretation Rules:

• **Why is a Lateral Flow Cassette INVALID if the Test Line (T) is positive but the Control Line (C) is absent?** Because the Control Line (immobilized anti-species secondary antibody, e.g., Goat anti-Mouse IgG) must ALWAYS capture the mobile gold-conjugated antibody to prove that capillary migration reached the end of the nitrocellulose strip and the conjugate did not aggregate non-specifically!

• **The High-Dose 'Hook Effect' (Prozone Phenomenon) in One-Step Sandwich ELISA / RDTs**: If a patient sample contains an **astronomically high concentration of antigen**, excess free antigen simultaneously saturates BOTH the mobile gold-detection antibodies AND the immobilized capture antibodies at the Test Line independently—preventing sandwich bridge formation and yielding a **False-Negative or paradoxically weak Test Line**! (*Fix*: Dilute the patient serum 1:10 or 1:100 and re-test!).

• **Western Blot vs. ELISA**: Indirect ELISA has high sensitivity (few false negatives, ideal for initial blood-bank screening), whereas Western Blot / Immunoblot separates antigens by MW first, offering superior **specificity** (eliminating false positives).
pathology: Clinical IVD Quality Control: In-Vitro Diagnostic (IVD) rapid cassettes and ELISA kits require strict validation of **Diagnostic Sensitivity** ($\text{TP} / [\text{TP} + \text{FN}]$), **Diagnostic Specificity** ($\text{TN} / [\text{TN} + \text{FP}]$), **Limit of Detection (LoD)**, and Accelerated Stability under controlled humidity (RH < 30% with silica desiccant for nitrocellulose cassettes).
lab_workbench: 4-Parameter Logistic (4PL) Sigmoidal Standard Curve Fitting & FACS Compensation: In ELISA, plotting $\text{OD}_{450}$ against $\log[\text{Antigen}]$ yields a sigmoidal curve whose inflection point ($\text{EC}_{50}$) provides the highest quantitative precision; in multi-color Flow Cytometry (FACS), spectral overlap between FITC and PE is corrected mathematically using single-stained **Compensation Controls**.
